questions.question: In 1851, who discovered the phenomenon of Eddy currents which flow in closed loops within conductors in planes perpendicular to the magnetic field?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Leon Foucault**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1851**, **Leon Foucault**, a **French** physicist, **discovered **the phenomenon of** Eddy currents**.
 
• He demonstrated that **when **a **conductor moves through a magnetic field or vice versa**, an **electric current is induced within the conductor**, forming closed loops perpendicular to the magnetic field.
 
• **These currents** are **known **as **Eddy currents** and can have various **effects**, including:
 
 
• **Generating heat**: The flow of Eddy currents within conductors results in energy loss as heat. This can be detrimental in some applications like transformers and motors.
 
• **Damping motion**: Eddy currents can induce a drag force on moving conductors in a magnetic field, slowing down their motion. This effect is used in magnetic brakes and damping mechanisms.
 
• **Creating repulsion forces**: Repulsive forces arise between a magnet and a conductor experiencing Eddy currents due to the interaction of their magnetic fields.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **British-American** inventor, practical experimenter, and music professor **David Edward Hughes** is well-known for his contributions to the **development **of the **printing telegraph **and the **microphone**.
 
• **American **physicist **Charles Hard Townes** worked on** quantum electronics **related to both **maser **and **laser devices**, as well as the theory and implementation of the maser, for which he was granted the foundational patent.
 
• **Nikola Tesla **was a **Serbian-American** inventor, futurist, and mechanical and electrical engineer.
 
 
• His contributions to the present **alternating current (AC) energy delivery system's design **are what made him most famous.

questions.question: Who, in the 1860s, undertook a thorough investigation of the gas laws expressing the relationships of pressure, temperature, and volume in carbon dioxide?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thomas Andrews.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thomas Andrews was an Irish chemist who made significant contributions to the study of gases.**
 
• In the 1860s, Andrews conducted a series of experiments on carbon dioxide gas and discovered the critical temperature and pressure of the gas.
 
• He also formulated the concept of the critical point, which is the temperature and pressure at which a gas and liquid are indistinguishable.
 
• Andrews' work on the gas laws of carbon dioxide was an important step towards understanding the behavior of gases in general.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Giulio Natta was an Italian chemist** who won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1963 for his work on high polymers.
 
• **John Dalton was an English chemist** who developed the atomic theory of matter and made important contributions to the study of gases.
 
• **Marguerite Perey **was a French physicist who discovered the element francium.

questions.question: Which experiment was designed to trace the motion of the earth through the 'luminiferous aether', a theoretical substance necessary for the transmission of light?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Michelson and Morley experiment.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Michelson and Morley experiment was designed to trace the earth's motion through the luminiferous aether, a theoretical substance necessary for transmitting light.**
 
• The experiment was conducted in **1887 by Albert Michelson and Edward Morley.**
 
• The experiment aimed to detect the relative motion of the earth and the luminiferous aether by measuring the speed of light in different directions.
 
• The experiment results were surprising as they showed that the speed of light was constant in all directions, which contradicted the prevailing theory of the existence of the luminiferous aether.
 
• The Michelson and Morley experiment paved the way for the development of Einstein's theory of relativity, which explained the behavior of light and the absence of the luminiferous aether.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maxwell and Hertz experiment: **This experiment was conducted by James Clerk Maxwell and Heinrich Hertz in the late 19th century to demonstrate the existence of electromagnetic waves.
 
• **Faraday and Henry experiment:** This experiment was conducted by Michael Faraday and Joseph Henry in the 19th century to study the phenomenon of electromagnetic induction.
 
• **Marconi and Thomson experiment: **This experiment was conducted by Guglielmo Marconi and Joseph John Thomson in the early 20th century to demonstrate the feasibility of wireless communication.

questions.question: An earthquake of magnitude ________ on the Richter scale has a hundred times more destructive energy than an earthquake of magnitude 4.
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

Earthquake: An earthquake is a sudden shaking or trembling of the earth which lasts for a very short time. It is caused by a disturbance deep inside the earth’s crust.

__
 
• The Richter scale was developed by **Charles F. Richter in 1935** to measure the magnitude of an earthquake.
 
• Like many other scales in science, the **Richter scale is not linear**. It is a logarithmic increase.
 
• The Richter scale is a base 10 logarithmic scale that is used to measure the magnitude of the earthquake.
 
• This means that an earthquake with magnitude 6 would be 10 times stronger than magnitude 5 and 100 times stronger than magnitude 4

Therefore, the** correct answer is scale 6.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**
